scenario: getAlertsToFire 是 Warehouse 的私有方法，只被已处于 synchronized(this) 内的 addStock 和 removeStock 调用。
scenario_en: getAlertsToFire is a private Warehouse method, called only from addStock and removeStock while they already hold synchronized(this).
q: 它自己还要不要再加一层同步？
q_en: Should it add its own layer of synchronization?
options: 不用，调用方已持锁，再加同步在非重入锁下反而会自锁
要，凡是读共享 map 的方法都必须自己加同步才安全
要，因为它会调用 listener，回调必须被锁保护起来
不用，因为它读到的 alertConfigs 是一份线程私有的拷贝
options_en: No — the caller already holds the lock, and re-locking would self-deadlock under a non-reentrant lock.
Yes — any method that reads a shared map must synchronize itself to be safe.
Yes — it invokes the listener, and that callback has to be protected by the lock.
No — the alertConfigs it reads is a thread-private copy.
optionExplanations: 锁已经在外层拿到，重复加锁没有新收益，还得依赖锁的可重入性。
私有方法不是入口，它的安全由唯一的调用路径保证而不是自己声明。
它只收集待触发的 listener，真正的回调在释放锁之后才执行。
它直接读的就是共享的 alertConfigs，并没有做任何拷贝。
optionExplanations_en: The lock is already held one frame up, so re-acquiring adds nothing and leans on reentrancy.
A private method is not an entry point; its safety comes from its single call path, not its own declaration.
It only collects the listeners to fire — the actual callback runs after the lock is released.
It reads the shared alertConfigs directly; no copy is made anywhere.
why: 私有方法的线程安全由调用约定保证：调用方全程持锁。代价是这条约定必须写清楚，否则以后有人从锁外调用它就破防。
why_en: The private method's thread safety rests on a calling convention — every caller holds the lock — so that convention has to be documented or a future caller breaks it.
tradeoff: 靠调用约定省一层锁 vs 方法自带同步更防呆
whenOtherWins: 如果这个方法以后要暴露成 public 供外部直接调用，它就必须自己加同步。

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一个线程可以重复获取自己已经持有的锁而不会卡死，如 Java 的 synchronized。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A reentrant lock lets the same thread acquire a lock it already holds without deadlocking, like Java's synchronized.

scenario: 为提高吞吐改成 per-product 锁，让不同产品真正并行，但 inventory 仍然是普通 HashMap。
scenario_en: To raise throughput you switch to per-product locks so different products truly run in parallel, but inventory is still a plain HashMap.
q: 为什么这时必须换成 ConcurrentHashMap？
q_en: Why must the map become a ConcurrentHashMap at this point?
options: 即使操作不同 key，HashMap 的扩容和桶管理也会被并发破坏
因为普通 HashMap 不支持用字符串 productId 当键
HashMap 在不同 key 上本来就是安全的，只是速度会慢一些
因为 ConcurrentHashMap 会自动按 productId 帮你加好每个产品的锁
options_en: Even for different keys, a HashMap's resizing and bucket bookkeeping get corrupted under concurrency.
A plain HashMap doesn't support string productIds as keys.
A HashMap is already safe across different keys; it's just somewhat slower.
ConcurrentHashMap automatically takes a per-product lock keyed by productId for you.
optionExplanations: resize 时数组和链表被同时改写，可能丢条目甚至读到损坏的结构。
键类型跟线程安全无关，HashMap 一直支持字符串键。
不同 key 落进同一个桶或同时触发 resize 就会互相踩，这个前提不成立。
它保护的是 map 结构本身，read-modify-write 仍要靠你自己的 productLocks。
optionExplanations_en: During a resize the array and its chains are rewritten concurrently, dropping entries or corrupting structure.
Key type has nothing to do with thread safety; HashMap has always accepted string keys.
Different keys can land in the same bucket or trigger a resize together, so that premise is false.
It protects the map structure itself; your read-modify-write still needs your own productLocks.
why: per-product 锁只保护单个产品的读改写，map 结构本身的并发修改要靠线程安全容器。代价是多一层容器开销和更难推理的边界。
why_en: Per-product locks only guard one product's read-modify-write, so the map structure itself needs a thread-safe container underneath.
tradeoff: 细粒度锁提高并发 vs 需要线程安全容器兜底结构安全
whenOtherWins: 仓库级单锁下所有访问本来就串行，普通 HashMap 完全够用，不必换容器。

termDefinitions.meaning: 线程安全的哈希表，内部保护自己的桶和扩容，多个线程可同时读写不同键。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A ConcurrentHashMap is a thread-safe hash table that guards its own buckets and resizing so threads can touch different keys at once.

termDefinitions.meaning: 哈希表元素变多时重新分配更大的数组并把所有条目搬过去。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Resizing allocates a larger array when a hash table grows and rehashes every entry into it.

scenario: per-product 锁存在 productLocks 这张 map 里，仓库上线几年会见过上百万个不同的 productId。
scenario_en: The per-product locks live in a productLocks map, and over a few years the warehouse will have seen millions of distinct productIds.
q: 这些锁对象该何时创建、何时删除？
q_en: When should a per-product lock object be created, and when removed?
options: 第一次见到该产品时创建，之后基本不回收，内存代价可接受
每次操作结束就把这把锁从 map 里删掉，避免内存增长
系统启动时按产品目录一次性把所有锁全部预先创建好
给每把锁配一个定时器，闲置超过一分钟就自动销毁并重建
options_en: Create one the first time you see the product and basically never reclaim it; the memory cost is fine.
Delete the lock from the map as soon as each operation finishes, to avoid unbounded growth.
Pre-create every lock at startup by walking the product catalog.
Give each lock a timer that destroys and recreates it after a minute of being idle.
optionExplanations: 一个锁对象只有几十字节，百万级产品也就几十 MB，换来的是不用做回收。
删除的瞬间可能有线程正要拿这把锁，随后两边会锁到不同对象上。
产品目录在本系统之外，服务只在收到 productId 时才知道它存在。
定时销毁把删除竞态变成周期性发生，问题更难复现也更难排查。
optionExplanations_en: A lock object is a few dozen bytes, so even millions of products cost tens of megabytes and no reclamation logic.
At the instant you delete it another thread may be about to acquire it, and the two then lock different objects.
The product catalog lives outside this system; the service learns a productId exists only when it arrives.
A timer turns the deletion race into a recurring event, making the bug harder to reproduce.
why: 安全回收锁很难，因为无法确定没有线程正要获取它；按需创建、只增不减是标准做法。代价是 productLocks 随见过的产品数单调增长。
why_en: Reclaiming a lock safely is hard because you can't prove no thread is about to grab it, so you create on first use and never remove.
tradeoff: 只增不减避开回收竞态 vs map 长期占用内存
whenOtherWins: 如果 productId 是一次性生成的（比如按批次），锁 map 会无界增长，就得做带引用计数的回收。

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一把大锁拆成按 key 分配的多把小锁，让不同 key 的操作并行。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Lock striping splits one big lock into many keyed locks so operations on different keys can run in parallel.

scenario: 结账占了 5 分钟的 reservation，清理任务每分钟扫一次过期占用，此刻支付回调才到达并调用 confirmReservation。
scenario_en: A checkout held a 5-minute reservation, a cleanup task sweeps expired ones every minute, and the payment callback only now calls confirmReservation.
q: confirmReservation 必须先做哪一步校验？
q_en: What must confirmReservation validate first?
options: 比较当前时间和 reservation.expiresAt，已过期就返回 false
确认 reserved[productId] 大于等于本次要确认的数量
检查这个 productId 上还有没有别的 reservation 正在排队等待
重新调用一次 checkAvailability，确认可售库存仍然够本次订单
options_en: Compare the current time with reservation.expiresAt and return false if it has expired.
Confirm that reserved[productId] is at least the quantity being confirmed.
Check whether any other reservation for this productId is still queued behind it.
Call checkAvailability again to confirm the sellable stock still covers this order.
optionExplanations: 过期的占用可能已被清理任务释放并卖给别人，直接扣减就会超卖。
这个计数在 reserve 和 release 里各自增减，不是确认时的判据。
别人的占用早就从可售数量里扣掉了，不影响本次能否确认。
预占的意义正是不必重查可售量，重查等于把 reservation 白做了。
optionExplanations_en: An expired hold may already have been released by the cleanup task and sold to someone else.
That counter is incremented on reserve and decremented on release; it isn't the check that matters at confirm time.
Other people's holds were already subtracted from the sellable pool, so they don't gate this confirm.
The whole point of reserving is not having to re-check availability; re-checking wastes the reservation.
why: reservation 是一份有到期时间的库存租约，过期后那批数量可能已被清理任务释放给别人。代价是卡在边界的合法支付会被拒。
why_en: A reservation is a lease with an expiry, and once it lapses the cleanup task may have already handed those units to someone else.
tradeoff: 严格校验过期防超卖 vs 放宽校验保住已付款订单
whenOtherWins: 如果没有清理任务、占用只能显式释放，过期时间就只是提示，可以不做这次校验。

termDefinitions.meaning: 创建 reservation 时算出的 currentTime + timeoutMs，超过它这份占用即失效。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: expiresAt is currentTime plus the timeout, computed when the reservation is created; past it, the hold is void.

termDefinitions.meaning: 周期性扫描 reservations、把已过期的调用 releaseReservation 放回可售池的后台线程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The cleanup task is a background loop that scans reservations and releases the expired ones back into the sellable pool.

scenario: reservation 超时设为 5 分钟，一笔订单在第 5 分 10 秒回调成功，而支付其实早在窗口内就已发起。
scenario_en: The reservation timeout is 5 minutes and an order's callback lands at 5 minutes 10 seconds, though the payment itself began inside the window.
q: 该不该给这类刚过期的占用一个宽限期？
q_en: Should a just-expired reservation get a grace period?
options: 该给：支付已在进行中，硬拒会白白丢掉一笔已收的钱
不该给：任何宽限都会让超时时间失去意义，必须一刀切
该给：把超时时间直接改成一小时，宽限期就不需要了
不该给：应当把清理任务改成每毫秒扫描一次，杜绝边界情况
options_en: Yes — payment is already in flight, and a hard rejection throws away money you've collected.
No — any grace period makes the timeout meaningless, so the cutoff must be absolute.
Yes — just raise the timeout to an hour and you won't need a grace period at all.
No — sweep for expired reservations every millisecond instead and the edge case disappears.
optionExplanations: 边界上的损失是真金白银，多放行几秒的超卖概率远小于丢单成本。
超时是为了释放僵尸占用，不是为了惩罚正在付款的用户。
一小时会让热门商品长时间不可售，等于把不可卖窗口放大十几倍。
扫描再密也消不掉边界，只会让清理任务自己长期占着仓库锁。
optionExplanations_en: The loss at the boundary is real revenue, and a few extra seconds of oversell risk costs far less.
The timeout exists to free zombie holds, not to punish a customer who is mid-payment.
An hour keeps hot items unsellable far longer, stretching the blocked window more than tenfold.
No sweep frequency removes the boundary; it just keeps the cleanup task holding the warehouse lock.
why: 超时长度和宽限期都是商业决策：一头是被抢走占用的用户，一头是没抢到货的用户。代价是宽限窗口内确认的订单有小概率真超卖。
why_en: Both the timeout and the grace period are business calls, balancing the customer who loses a hold against the customer who never got stock.
tradeoff: 严格超时保公平 vs 宽限期保成交
whenOtherWins: 限量发售这类强调公平的场景，宁可拒掉迟到的确认，也不让超时的人插队。

termDefinitions.meaning: 超时之后再留一小段时间，允许支付已在进行中的 reservation 仍被确认。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A grace period is a short window after expiry during which a reservation whose payment is already in flight can still be confirmed.

scenario: 库存已从源仓扣出、交给 Transfer 对象持有，卡车在路上要跑 3-5 天。
scenario_en: The stock has left the source warehouse and is held by a Transfer object while the truck spends three to five days on the road.
q: 到货和运输取消这两条路径分别怎么收尾？
q_en: How do the arrival path and the cancellation path each finish?
options: 到货把数量加到目标仓并删除 Transfer；取消则把数量退回源仓
到货把数量加到目标仓，取消时直接丢弃这条 Transfer 记录
到货和取消都只改 Transfer 的状态字段，库存就留在 Transfer 里不动
在途期间目标仓就已计入这批库存，收尾只需要删掉 Transfer 记录
options_en: Arrival credits the destination and deletes the Transfer; cancellation returns the units to the source.
Arrival credits the destination, and cancellation simply discards the Transfer record.
Both paths just flip a status field on the Transfer and the stock stays inside it.
The destination already counts the units while in transit, so finishing just deletes the Transfer.
optionExplanations: 两条路径都让这批数量回到某个 Warehouse，系统总量始终守恒。
丢弃记录等于把货物凭空销账，取消一次就少一批库存。
库存永远停在 Transfer 里，目标仓拿不到货，可售量再也不恢复。
在途期间两边都不该可售，提前计入会让目标仓卖出还没到的货。
optionExplanations_en: Both paths land the units back in some Warehouse, so the system total stays conserved.
Discarding the record writes the goods off into nothing; one cancellation silently destroys stock.
The units stay parked in the Transfer forever, so the destination never receives them.
Neither side should count in-transit units as sellable, or the destination sells goods that haven't arrived.
why: Transfer 是临时持有者：completeTransfer 把数量交给目标仓后删除记录，取消则把数量退回源仓。代价是多一个实体和它的清理逻辑。
why_en: The Transfer is a temporary holder: completing it hands the units to the destination and drops the record, while cancelling returns them to the source.
tradeoff: 在途实体让总量随时可核对 vs 瞬移模型代码更少
whenOtherWins: 如果调拨是同一栋楼内几分钟完成，双锁瞬移模型足够，不必引入 Transfer 实体。

termDefinitions.meaning: Warehouse 和 Transfer 共同实现的接口，表示任何可以持有库存的地方。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: InventoryHolder is the interface shared by Warehouse and Transfer, representing anywhere stock can live.

termDefinitions.meaning: 已离开源仓、尚未到达目标仓的那批数量，不可售但仍计入系统总量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: In-transit inventory has left the source but not yet arrived: not sellable, but still counted in the system total.
